- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 5% of spike magnitude.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a “mean reversion” bias: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: higher sentiment = higher weight on recent data.
